claims.text: Standard deposition produces a relatively coarse FeNiCrCoCu coating with comparatively low twin and defect density.
Increasing the cooling rate during deposition or applying a rapid quench produces an ultra-fine-grained FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Increasing the cooling rate produces abundant twins and grain boundaries in the coating.
Rapidly processed FeNiCrCoCu develops an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer mediates dynamic amorphization during sliding.
Dynamic amorphization contributes to formation of the ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Grain boundaries and twin interfaces obstruct dislocation motion.
The refined microstructure mitigates inverse Hall-Petch behavior.
Mitigating inverse Hall-Petch behavior reduces local shear localization and plastic deformation during sliding.
An ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer improves wear resistance.
Increasing the cooling rate will lower the wear volume or wear rate relative to the baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Increasing the cooling rate will reduce the severity of microscopic deformation during sliding.
Reduced microscopic deformation will appear as fewer or smaller stress drops or deformation events.
The predicted mechanism and outcomes apply above approximately 400–500 °C, where thermal activation significantly contributes to microstructural evolution.
The magnitude of wear reduction and microstructural refinement depends sensitively on cooling rate and other processing variables.
The temperature at which the proposed mechanism becomes dominant over other high-temperature effects is not yet determined.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the near-surface layer mediates dynamic amorphization, while the structural-mediator field says that the layer forms as a result of dynamic amorphization. This makes the causal ordering circular or inconsistent.

The predicted causal outcome requires reduced wear after formation of the refined structure, but the stated rule only falsifies the hypothesis when both wear fails to improve and the structure fails to form. Thus, formation of the proposed mediator without reduced wear would violate the prediction but would not satisfy the stated falsification rule.
